purpose: Define the practical framework target: convert an upstream candidate corpus into a supported language-model training release or an explicit abstention decision.

mission.input: candidate corpus from upstream collection with retained provenance when available
mission.output: full curated pool plus an optional budgeted training subset, scoped release with caveats, rejection, quarantine, or explicit abstention
mission.not_guaranteed: The framework does not guarantee that every candidate corpus can be made useful for training.
mission.primary_success_condition: Hard curation must retain all usable and policy-eligible data. Only when a training budget is constrained must a selected subset beat matched equal-token baselines under the frozen External Evaluation Protocol while satisfying retention, safety, contamination, and coverage guardrails.

validity.claim_boundary: Hard usability gate, not semantic usefulness or data quality.

selection_value.claim_boundary: Observable information-density, structural-usefulness, and boilerplate-risk evidence for budget allocation. It is not intrinsic or ground-truth quality, has no Stage-B hard-reject authority, and need not reduce a usable corpus.

quality.claim_boundary: Legacy runtime and artifact alias only. Quality is not a separate intrinsic construct and must not authorize rejection.

redundancy.claim_boundary: Raw and canonical-content exact duplicates are gates. Fuzzy near-duplicate and saturation evidence are soft Stage-C signals until independent precision and useful-data-dropout gates pass. Useful recurrence must be preserved.

coverage.stage: Stage C support and External Evaluation validation
coverage.claim_boundary: Source, style, content-type, path, and cluster support. Domain or semantic coverage is claimed only when metadata supports it.

stage_c.name: optional_budget_constrained_chunk_selection
stage_c.activation: Run only when an explicit training-token or compute budget is smaller than the full curated pool. Otherwise emit retain_all.
forbidden: fixed rejection or selection quotas presented as quality decisions
treating budget-not-selected records as rejected or low quality

invariants: Every Stage-B-pass non-quarantined record belongs to the full curated pool.
Budget-not-selected is not rejection and is not a low-quality label.
Retain-all is a valid expected outcome when the full curated pool fits the declared budget.
No fixed rejection quota or target reduction ratio is allowed.
Uncertain safety cases are quarantined; uncertain selection-value cases remain retained unless an independent hard gate applies.

required_before_claiming_operational_rea: split harmful duplication from useful recurrence
preserve concise but useful examples, tests, bug fixes, and API usage chunks
separate AST richness from learnable code usefulness
cap repository, path, and template concentration
report selected-vs-budget-not-selected feature shifts before External Evaluation without labeling either side as ground-truth quality
emit failure diagnoses when curated does not beat the Stage-B-random control

forbidden_claims: The framework measures intrinsic data quality.
A high Stage-C Quality or selection-value proxy score proves training usefulness.
Curation must always reduce the input corpus.
A budget-not-selected record is low quality or rejected.
A positive result on an already curated dataset proves raw-corpus operation.
External Evaluation outcomes can be used to tune Stage-C for the same frozen cycle.
Every arbitrary candidate corpus can be transformed into a useful training dataset.
allowed_claim_template: The framework removes or quarantines only records covered by explicit hard rules, preserves the remaining full curated pool, and uses frozen pre-outcome selection-value, redundancy, and coverage evidence to construct an optional budgeted training subset whose downstream effect is validated by the External Evaluation Protocol.
utility_scope: External Evaluation Protocol only; never Stage-C selector objective
